question: Why are wrinkled bed sheets a skin risk for an unconscious patient?

options.A: They interfere with taking core body temperature.
options.B: They block all blood flow to the skin.
options.C: They create friction and rubbing that damage the skin.
options.D: They trap extra body heat and cause dehydration.

explanation: Creases and rough bed sheets rub against the skin, breaking down outer layers and leading to pressure sores. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T1#BMP120_U5_T1_h4)

question: What is the purpose of creating a toe pleat in the top bed linen?

options.A: To prevent pressure and foot drop on the patient's toes
options.B: To allow extra airflow underneath the bed covers
options.C: To make it easier for the patient to pull the covers up
options.D: To hide unsightly wrinkles at the bottom of the mattress

explanation: Heavy bed linens pressing down on the feet can cause toe pressure and lead to foot drop, which a loose toe pleat successfully prevents. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the main reason for giving antibiotics before the lab culture results come back?

options.A: To numb the surgical incision so the patient feels no physical pain
options.B: To rapidly control suspected bacterial growth while waiting for lab results
options.C: To replace the routine practice of aseptic wound dressing changes
options.D: To permanently eliminate the need for any future surgical wound care

explanation: Starting medications early helps fight off likely bacteria right away while everyone waits for the final lab report. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is the main job of clotting factors in the blood?

options.A: To transport iron molecules directly to the bone marrow
options.B: To sequentially activate one another and form a stable fibrin mesh
options.C: To actively destroy red blood cells near the injury site
options.D: To maintain high blood pressure throughout the vascular tree

explanation: Clotting factors work in a chain reaction to turn soluble proteins into solid fibrin threads that reinforce the platelet plug. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T9#BMP111_U5_T9_h3)

question: What specific structures regulate blood flow directly into individual capillary networks?

options.A: Precapillary sphincters
options.B: Venous valves
options.C: Lymphatic nodes
options.D: Cardiac Purkinje fibers

explanation: Precapillary sphincters are rings of smooth muscle at the junction of arterioles and capillaries that control local blood entry. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T14#BMP111_U5_T14_h6)

question: A midwife in a health center notices a sudden rise in cholera cases in the local market. What immediate action should she take?

options.A: Report the outbreak to local public health authorities for prompt action
options.B: Refer all affected patients abroad for specialized treatment
options.C: Close the clinic permanently until the rainy season ends
options.D: Wait until the end of the year to include it in the routine budget

explanation: Timely disease reporting to public health agencies allows the government to send help quickly and prevent a wider outbreak. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T7#BMP110_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why do midwives move the limbs of an unconscious patient through gentle stretches?

options.A: To keep joints from getting stiff and maintain flexibility
options.B: To make the patient start moving on their own
options.C: To replace the need for turning them in bed
options.D: To build up the patient's muscle strength

explanation: Since the patient cannot move themselves, gentle passive stretches keep the joints flexible and stop contractures. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T1#BMP120_U5_T1_h7)

question: How do skeletal muscles help move lymph through the deep vessels?

options.A: Muscles pull directly on the lymph node capsules to empty their contents
options.B: Muscles release heat that turns lymph into a gas for easier travel
options.C: Contracting muscles compress the lymph vessels, pushing fluid past one-way valves
options.D: Skeletal muscles pump blood directly into the initial lymphatic capillaries

explanation: The skeletal muscle pump squeezes surrounding lymph vessels during movement, driving lymph upward through the one-way internal valves. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T1#BMP111_U6_T1_h6)

question: Which part of the nerve cell does bupivacaine block to stop pain signals?

options.A: Potassium leakage pathways
options.B: Calcium storage vesicles
options.C: Voltage-gated sodium channels
options.D: Chloride transport proteins

explanation: Bupivacaine binds to voltage-gated sodium channels to stop sodium from entering, which prevents pain signals from travelling along the nerve. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T7#BMP213_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is the main job of sodium bicarbonate in the body?

options.A: Buffering metabolic acidosis
options.B: Dilating the bronchial airways
options.C: Increasing heart rate directly
options.D: Suppressing neonatal seizures

explanation: Sodium bicarbonate acts as an alkaline agent that neutralizes excess hydrogen ions to help correct metabolic acidosis. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T5#BMP213_U4_T5_h1)

question: What is the classic newborn arm posture seen in Erb's palsy after a difficult shoulder delivery?

options.A: Ape hand flattening
options.B: Waiter's tip posture
options.C: Dropped wrist posture
options.D: Claw hand deformity

explanation: Injury to the upper nerves of the arm plexus makes the shoulder turn inward, causing the arm to hang limply in a specific position. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T10#BMP111_U3_T10_h7)

question: A senior midwife takes time to listen to a junior colleague's concerns and offers encouraging feedback. Which management function is she demonstrating?

options.A: Controlling
options.B: Organizing
options.C: Planning
options.D: Directing

explanation: Listening, encouraging, and providing constructive feedback are core parts of effective leadership and direction. [learn more](BMP312_U1_T5#BMP312_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the main way oxygen and carbon dioxide move across cell membranes?

options.A: Pressure and diffusion gradients
options.B: Direct electrical attraction
options.C: Active transport by cellular pumps
options.D: Osmotic pull of plasma proteins

explanation: Gases move naturally from areas of higher pressure to areas of lower pressure without needing energy from the cells. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which two primary hormones directly drive the cyclic changes in the endometrial lining?

options.A: Insulin and cortisol
options.B: Estrogen and progesterone
options.C: Oxytocin and prolactin
options.D: Thyroxine and calcitonin

explanation: Ovarian hormones, specifically estrogen and progesterone, act directly on the uterine tissue to orchestrate the phases of the endometrial cycle. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T5#BMP210_U2_T5_h1)

question: What main problem caused the highest number of deaths among soldiers when Florence Nightingale first arrived at the Scutari hospital?

options.A: Poor environmental and sanitary conditions
options.B: Severe lack of surgical supplies
options.C: A sudden shortage of trained military doctors
options.D: Direct gunshot wounds from enemy battles

explanation: Most soldiers in Scutari died from infectious diseases caused by filth, crowding, and lack of clean water rather than direct combat injuries. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T6#BMP110_U3_T6_h1)

question: What is the main job of the touch receptors found in the skin?

options.A: Holding the outer skin layer to the muscle below
options.B: Helping the body cool down by making sweat
options.C: Producing melanin to protect against the sun
options.D: Turning touch and temperature into electrical signals for the brain

explanation: Skin receptors specialize in converting physical feelings from the environment into nerve signals that travel to the brain. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T6#BMP111_U4_T6_h1)

question: Why is bone considered a living tissue rather than a dry, lifeless structure?

options.A: It grows continuously without ever stopping.
options.B: It requires constant food to maintain its weight.
options.C: It produces red blood cells entirely on its own.
options.D: It contains active cells, blood vessels, and nerves.

explanation: Bone has blood vessels, nerves, and living cells that constantly work to repair and remodel the tissue. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T1#BMP111_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why must a patient remove all dark nail polish before being transferred to the operating theatre?

options.A: It interferes with the accurate reading of the pulse oximeter
options.B: It can react chemically with the cleaning agents used for the skin
options.C: It increases the risk of the patient developing an allergic reaction
options.D: It makes it difficult for the surgeon to check for surgical site bleeding

explanation: Pulse oximeters shine light through the nail bed to measure oxygen levels; dark polish blocks this light and gives false readings. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T2#BMP120_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why is knowing how a bone injury happened useful when caring for a patient?

options.A: It replaces the need for an X-ray examination
options.B: It prevents infection from developing later
options.C: It gives clues about the severity of the damage
options.D: It dictates the exact type of surgery required

explanation: Understanding how an injury happened helps healthcare providers figure out how bad the damage might be. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T5#BMP110_U7_T5_h1)

question: What should a midwife do if a patient is too weak to cough up sputum?

options.A: Collect ordinary saliva and label it as sputum
options.B: Wait several days until the patient regains strength
options.C: Scrape the back of the patient's throat with a cotton swab
options.D: Consult the medical officer for assistance like nebulized saline or physiotherapy

explanation: Weak patients often need clinical support like nebulization or physical therapy to help clear respiratory secretions. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T4#BMP110_U6_T4_h3)

question: How do cartilaginous joints compare to synovial joints in terms of movement?

options.A: They allow a wider range of circular movement
options.B: They allow much less movement than synovial joints
options.C: They allow complete rotation in all directions
options.D: They do not differ in their range of movement at all

explanation: Because cartilage binds them firmly without a fluid-filled space, these joints permit only slight movement. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T15#BMP111_U2_T15_h1)

question: Which substance found in unrefined grains can bind to calcium in the gut and increase the risk of rickets?

options.A: Phytates
options.B: Hemoglobin
options.C: Lactic acid
options.D: Glucose

explanation: Phytates present in unrefined grains bind to minerals like calcium and prevent proper absorption in the intestines. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T20#BMP111_U2_T20_h3)

question: What is an important early warning sign of circulation problems in a patient with a fresh leg cast?

options.A: Severe pain that does not go away with pain medication
options.B: A slight itchiness on the skin just under the cast edge
options.C: A small amount of clear yellow drainage on the outer surface
options.D: Mild warmth felt on the surface of the plaster material

explanation: Disproportionate, unrelenting pain is often the first warning sign of rising pressure inside the cast, such as in compartment syndrome. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T3#BMP216_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which anatomical plane should be aligned when positioning a patient for an accurate height measurement?

options.A: Sagittal midline plane
options.B: Coronal facial plane
options.C: Transverse pelvic plane
options.D: Frankfort horizontal plane

explanation: Aligning the line of sight so that the ear canal and eye socket are level keeps the head in the correct upright position. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T3#BMP110_U6_T3_h3)

question: Who must officially confirm and certify death before last offices can begin?

options.A: The mortuary attendant
options.B: A registered midwife
options.C: A qualified medical doctor
options.D: The head of the nursing unit

explanation: Legal confirmation of death must always be carried out by a physician before nurses or midwives begin post-mortem care. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T5#BMP120_U5_T5_h1)

question: Why is keeping accurate notes on bones and muscles important in clinical care?

options.A: It guarantees that the mother will have a normal spontaneous delivery
options.B: It replaces the need to talk directly with the pregnant client
options.C: It ensures safe continuity of care and guides timely referrals
options.D: It eliminates all possible risks of postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Clear notes allow all healthcare team members to track progress and refer clients for specialized care when needed. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T1#BMP216_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the main difference between the front (anterior) and back (posterior) lobes of the pituitary gland?

options.A: The posterior lobe controls basal metabolic rate, while the anterior lobe regulates only uterine contractions
options.B: The posterior lobe produces oxytocin independently, while the anterior lobe has no endocrine function
options.C: The anterior lobe synthesizes its own hormones, while the posterior lobe stores and releases hypothalamic hormones
options.D: The anterior lobe connects directly to the optic chiasm, while the posterior lobe sits outside the skull

explanation: Oxytocin and ADH are manufactured in the hypothalamus and simply stored and released by the posterior pituitary, unlike anterior hormones. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T1#BMP121_U4_T1_h2)

question: Which joint condition is caused by an autoimmune reaction that attacks the synovial membrane?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Osteoarthritis
options.C: Bursitis inflammation
options.D: Simple tendonitis

explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis happens when the body's immune system mistakenly attacks its own synovial membranes, leading to painful inflammation. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T17#BMP111_U2_T17_h7)

question: What structural feature of the pelvis causes the baby to curve forward as it moves down the birth canal?

options.A: The prominent ischial spines in the mid-pelvis
options.B: The movable coccyx at the pelvic outlet
options.C: The wide transverse diameter of the pelvic brim
options.D: The short front wall and long back wall

explanation: The shallow pubic bone in front combined with the deep sacrum in the back forces the baby to curve forward during descent. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T2#BMP210_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why do healthy bones need both collagen fibers and mineral crystals?

options.A: Collagen stores calcium while minerals protect the bone marrow
options.B: Minerals act as a fuel source while collagen provides joint lubrication
options.C: Minerals prevent blood loss while collagen produces red blood cells
options.D: Collagen provides flexibility while minerals provide rigid strength

explanation: The organic collagen prevents the bone from being too brittle, while the inorganic minerals prevent it from being too flexible. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T2#BMP111_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why are the bulky muscles that move the fingers located in the forearm instead of inside the hand?

options.A: To protect the delicate bones of the carpal tunnel
options.B: To keep the hand light and nimble for delicate tasks
options.C: Because blood supply cannot reach the palm easily
options.D: To allow the radial nerve to wrap around the wrist

explanation: Placing heavy muscle bellies in the forearm and connecting them with long tendons keeps the hand lightweight for precise grip. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T10#BMP111_U3_T10_h5)

question: Which of the following bones is NOT considered part of the flat bone category?

options.A: Ilium
options.B: Tibia
options.C: Parietal bone
options.D: Sternum

explanation: The tibia is a long bone of the lower leg, whereas the sternum, parietal bone, and ilium are all flat bones. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T5#BMP111_U2_T5_h3)

question: In the ABCDE primary survey framework, what does the letter 'C' stand for?

options.A: Coughing
options.B: Circulation
options.C: Contraction
options.D: Coma

explanation: In emergency assessment, C stands for circulation, checking pulses, bleeding, and perfusion. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T1#BMP110_U7_T1_h4)

question: A woman who just delivered twins has severe bleeding and trouble with her blood clotting. Which product should the midwife expect to give?

options.A: Fresh frozen plasma
options.B: Normal saline solution
options.C: Packed red blood cells
options.D: Washed platelets alone

explanation: Fresh frozen plasma is rich in coagulation factors, making it the correct choice to correct active bleeding caused by clotting factor deficiencies. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T8#BMP111_U5_T8_h1)

question: What is the normal pH range for arterial blood in humans?
explanation: Normal arterial blood pH is kept strictly between 7.35 and 7.45 to keep body chemistry working properly. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T4#BMP121_U3_T4_h6)

question: How does a midwife demonstrate the primary health care principle of equity?

options.A: Prioritizing wealthy community members who can donate to the clinic
options.B: Ensuring remote villages receive the same attention as urban centers
options.C: Giving free medications only to patients who visit the main city hospital
options.D: Limiting antenatal education sessions to educated women only

explanation: Equity means fair distribution of health resources so that vulnerable and remote populations are not left behind. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T10#BMP110_U5_T10_h2)

question: A patient is admitted with typhoid fever. Which statement represents her nursing diagnosis?

options.A: Prescription of intravenous ciprofloxacin
options.B: Hyperthermia related to systemic infection
options.C: Scheduled blood test for widal reaction
options.D: Salmonella typhi bacterial infection confirmed

explanation: The body temperature elevation in response to the infection is the human response addressed by the nursing diagnosis. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T3#BMP120_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the main focus of the fetal period compared to the earlier embryonic period?

options.A: Cleavage division of the single-celled zygote
options.B: Initial formation of the three germ layers
options.C: Growth and functional maturity of organs
options.D: Establishment of the primitive streak

explanation: After the organs are formed in the embryonic stage, the fetal stage is all about growing larger and helping those organ systems mature so they can work. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T5#BMP210_U4_T5_h3)

question: How do basic infection control measures like hand hygiene support antimicrobial stewardship?

options.A: By preventing infections from spreading, reducing the need for drug therapy
options.B: By directly neutralizing resistant bacterial enzymes on the skin surface
options.C: By shortening the time required for laboratory culture results
options.D: By increasing the absorption rate of oral antibiotics in the gut

explanation: Stopping the spread of germs means fewer people get sick in the first place, which naturally cuts down the total number of antibiotics needed. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T1#BMP124_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which movement turns the sole of the foot inward?

options.A: Eversion
options.B: Pronation
options.C: Inversion
options.D: Dorsiflexion

explanation: Inversion turns the sole of the foot inward toward the middle, while eversion turns it outward. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T17#BMP111_U2_T17_h6)

question: Which cell type in the deepest layer of the epidermis helps detect light touch by connecting with nerve endings?

options.A: Langerhans cells
options.B: Merkel cells
options.C: Melanocytes
options.D: Fibroblasts

explanation: Merkel cells form touch receptors that link up with sensory nerve fibers in the skin. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T1#BMP111_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why do busy wards use structured daily routines?

options.A: They help coordinate clinical activities and ensure tasks are not missed
options.B: They allow doctors to avoid visiting patients during morning hours
options.C: They prevent nurses from ever needing to communicate with each other
options.D: They completely eliminate the possibility of unexpected patient emergencies

explanation: Routines create a predictable flow for medication administration, meal times, and clinical reviews. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T1#BMP110_U2_T1_h5)

question: Where is a major symphysis joint located in the human pelvis?

options.A: Pubic symphysis
options.B: Sacroiliac capsule
options.C: Obturator membrane
options.D: Acetabular labrum

explanation: The pubic symphysis joins the left and right pubic bones at the midline of the pelvis. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T15#BMP111_U2_T15_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of an independent midwifery action?

options.A: Ordering a blood transfusion for severe anemia in pregnancy
options.B: Demonstrating proper breastfeeding positioning to a new mother
options.C: Administering prescribed intravenous magnesium sulfate for eclampsia
options.D: Performing an emergency episiotomy during second stage labor

explanation: Teaching breastfeeding techniques falls within the independent scope of professional midwifery practice without needing a doctor's order. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T4#BMP120_U1_T4_h4)

question: What does the first clear tapping sound heard through the stethoscope represent during blood pressure measurement?

options.A: Pulse pressure
options.B: Diastolic pressure
options.C: Mean arterial pressure
options.D: Systolic pressure

explanation: The onset of Korotkoff sounds, marked by the first tapping sound, corresponds to the systolic blood pressure. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T2#BMP110_U6_T2_h5)

question: What do we call it when a blastocyst implants outside the main uterine cavity, such as in the fallopian tube?

options.A: Placenta accreta
options.B: Hydatidiform mole
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Ectopic pregnancy

explanation: Any pregnancy that implants outside the uterus is called an ectopic pregnancy, with the fallopian tubes being the most common spot. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T4#BMP210_U4_T4_h6)

question: Which imaging scan is commonly used to clearly see blood flow blockages in the lungs?

options.A: Routine bedside pelvic transvaginal scan
options.B: Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain
options.C: Computed tomography pulmonary angiography
options.D: Standard abdominal obstetric ultrasound scan

explanation: This specific CT scan uses contrast dye to take pictures that directly show blood clots inside the lung arteries. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T9#BMP125_U2_T9_h5)

question: What does the term 'Golden Hour' mean in emergency care?

options.A: The time required to complete a full nursing care plan
options.B: The first sixty minutes after a critical injury or medical crisis
options.C: The designated visiting hour for relatives in the maternity ward
options.D: The time it takes for a baby to take its first breath after birth

explanation: The golden hour is the critical time frame where rapid medical intervention gives the highest chance of survival. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T1#BMP110_U7_T1_h2)

question: Why can an infection in the accessory glands lead to male infertility?

options.A: It changes the fluid balance and harms sperm movement
options.B: It stops the testes from producing any testosterone
options.C: It causes the penis to become completely flaccid
options.D: It permanently closes the muscular vas deferens

explanation: Infections alter the normal chemical composition of seminal fluid, making it difficult for sperm to survive or swim properly. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T3#BMP210_U3_T3_h6)

question: A postpartum mother has acute pain from an episiotomy and ineffective breathing due to a pulmonary issue. Which diagnosis should take top priority?

options.A: Deficient knowledge of baby care
options.B: Risk for constipation
options.C: Acute pain from episiotomy
options.D: Ineffective breathing pattern

explanation: Airway and breathing are primary physiological survival needs that always override pain management in priority. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T3#BMP120_U1_T3_h7)

question: What happens if team members do not synchronize their lifting movements with a count?

options.A: The transfer will finish much faster than normally expected
options.B: The patient will feel more relaxed during the transfer procedure
options.C: Uneven weight distribution can injure workers and drop the patient
options.D: The mechanical lift will automatically correct the timing error

explanation: Uncoordinated lifting shifts the load abruptly onto one or two workers, causing muscle strain and fall risks. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T6#BMP110_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why use an intravenous route instead of oral during an obstetric emergency?

options.A: Oral medications are completely prohibited in all maternity wards
options.B: Intravenous medications reach the bloodstream and act much faster
options.C: Digestive juices make oral drugs completely harmless to the body
options.D: Intravenous injections cause zero discomfort compared to swallowing pills

explanation: When every second counts, such as managing severe bleeding after birth, injecting drugs straight into a vein provides an immediate therapeutic effect. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T3#BMP120_U2_T3_h1)

question: What causes the rattling breathing sound often heard in actively dying patients?

options.A: Complete blockage of the nose by nasal secretions
options.B: Rapid expansion of air trapped inside the chest wall
options.C: Sudden severe infection inside the lung tissue
options.D: Inability to clear and swallow normal oral secretions

explanation: As swallowing reflexes fail, saliva and mucus pool in the upper airway, producing the sound often referred to as the death rattle. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T2#BMP120_U5_T2_h3)

question: Which healthcare worker commonly manages a standard primary health clinic in Nigeria?

options.A: Community Health Extension Worker
options.B: Pharmacist specialist
options.C: Consultant surgeon
options.D: Radiology technician

explanation: CHEWs form the backbone of staffing for primary health clinics and basic health centres across rural and semi-urban settlements. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h4)

question: Where do touch and pain signals from the skin finally go so a person can feel them?

options.A: The somatosensory cortex in the brain
options.B: The sympathetic trunk along the spine
options.C: The motor cortex that controls movement
options.D: The front part of the spinal cord

explanation: Sensory signals travel up the spinal cord and brainstem to end in the somatosensory cortex, which lets a person consciously feel the sensation. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T6#BMP111_U4_T6_h2)

question: Which of the following is an example of a medical diagnosis?

options.A: Risk for infection
options.B: Severe pre-eclampsia
options.C: Acute pain
options.D: Ineffective breastfeeding

explanation: Severe pre-eclampsia is a distinct medical disease condition, whereas the others describe human responses managed by nursing care. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T3#BMP120_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is a major advantage of involving patients in their shift handover?

options.A: They pay their hospital bills faster
options.B: They take over medication administration duties
options.C: They can write the official nursing notes for the shift
options.D: They can help catch errors in their treatment plan

explanation: Patients know their bodies well and can immediately point out if something discussed does not match their experience. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T5#BMP110_U3_T5_h4)

question: What safety device should you use instead of bare fingers when cleaning an unconscious patient's teeth?

options.A: Wooden mixing stick
options.B: Plastic feeding tube
options.C: Padded tongue blade
options.D: Metal surgical clamp

explanation: Using a padded tongue blade prevents finger injuries if the patient suddenly closes their jaw due to an involuntary reflex. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T3#BMP110_U5_T3_h4)

question: Why are safety straps placed across a patient on a stretcher?

options.A: To make the stretcher lighter to carry
options.B: To restrict the patient from speaking during the trip
options.C: To prevent the patient from falling off during rough movement
options.D: To keep the patient's blood pressure artificially high

explanation: Straps hold the casualty securely in place when the vehicle navigates potholes, bumps, or sharp corners. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T11#BMP110_U7_T11_h4)

question: What happens first to the fetus if a pregnant woman has severely low blood pressure?

options.A: Less oxygen reaches the placenta, which can cause fetal distress
options.B: The baby's birth weight and lung maturity suddenly increase
options.C: Blood flow direction in the umbilical cord reverses
options.D: Waste production stops inside the amniotic sac

explanation: Low maternal blood pressure reduces blood flow to the placenta, lowering the pressure gradient and starving the baby of needed oxygen. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T4#BMP121_U1_T4_h7)

question: What happens when stool sits inside the rectum for too long without being passed?

options.A: The rectum stops sending nerve signals
options.B: It turns back into liquid chyme
options.C: More water is absorbed from it
options.D: The body digests the remaining waste

explanation: The lining of the large intestine continuously pulls water out of its contents, so delaying defecation allows more fluid to leave the stool, making it dry and hard. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T5#BMP121_U2_T5_h2)

question: What two main parts join together to form a complete haemoglobin molecule?

options.A: Heme and globin chains
options.B: Plasma and platelets
options.C: Iron and white blood cells
options.D: Albumin and reticulocytes

explanation: Haemoglobin is built by combining iron-containing heme rings with protein globin chains. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T5#BMP111_U5_T5_h4)

question: What should a midwife do when a drug dosage order written in a case note looks unclear?

options.A: Guess the correct amount based on the patient's body weight
options.B: Ask another junior student to make the final decision
options.C: Skip giving that specific dose for the day entirely
options.D: Clarify the order with the prescriber before giving the drug

explanation: Never guess an unclear order because doing so can easily cause a severe medication overdose or error. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T7#BMP110_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary tool used by midwives to monitor the progress of labor and detect delays early?

options.B: The partograph

question: Why does sperm need the secretions produced by the accessory glands?

options.D: To help the body filter waste products

question: Which blood test result usually points to an active bacterial infection in a post-op patient?

options.A: Elevated red blood cell count
options.B: Decreased platelet aggregation rate
options.C: Decreased total serum protein level
options.D: Elevated white blood cell count

question: What action does the skin take when the body needs to release excess internal heat?

options.A: Vasodilation of dermal blood vessels

options.D: Decreasing overall sweat gland activity

question: What is the thin layer that anchors epithelial tissue to the connective tissue underneath?

options.A: Basement membrane
options.B: Muscular layer
options.C: Endothelial wall
options.D: Serous membrane

question: What is the primary energy source for secondary active transport?

options.A: An existing electrochemical gradient
options.B: Passive diffusion of water molecules

question: Why is the QRS complex much taller and sharper than the P wave on an ECG recording?

options.D: The QRS complex records repolarization instead of depolarization

question: A patient loses their spleen in an accident. What health step is most important for them afterward?

options.A: Undergoing weekly blood transfusions to maintain volume
options.B: Receiving specific vaccinations against bacterial infections
options.C: Taking daily high-dose iron supplements to replace lost stores
options.D: Avoiding all physical exercise to prevent internal bleeding

question: Which health condition can slow down white blood cells and help bacteria grow faster in a surgical wound?

options.A: Short duration of anesthesia
options.B: Mild iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: Uncontrolled diabetes mellitus
options.D: Well-managed essential hypertension

explanation: High blood sugar levels make it harder for infection-fighting white blood cells to work properly, creating an environment where bacteria thrive. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T6#BMP120_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is the specific role of troponin in muscle contraction?

options.A: It acts as an anchor protein that fastens the thick filaments directly to the M-line.

question: Which specific nail condition is commonly linked to severe iron deficiency anemia in pregnant women?

options.A: Transverse deep ridges
options.B: Thickened fungal nails
options.C: Spoon-shaped nails
options.D: Bluish nail beds

question: Why is continued observation necessary even after a patient recovers from an asphyxiic episode?

options.A: The body completely stops producing urine after oxygen lack

question: Which body parts receive the highest concentration of oxygen in the fetal circulation?

options.A: The brain and upper extremities
options.B: The lower limbs and pelvic organs
options.C: The urinary bladder and kidneys
options.D: The gastrointestinal tract and liver

explanation: Because of how the foramen ovale and ductus venosus route blood, the head and arms get the freshest oxygen supply. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T4#BMP210_U5_T4_h6)

question: Which specific bone cell type is responsible for breaking down or resorbing bone matrix?

options.A: Osteoblast
options.B: Osteogenic cell

options.D: Osteoclast

explanation: Osteoclasts use enzymes and acids to dissolve bone minerals and matrix, which is a necessary process for remodeling and healing. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T2#BMP111_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is a major role of amniotic fluid during mid-to-late pregnancy?

options.A: Providing all the necessary dietary protein for the growing fetus
options.B: Producing hormones that trigger the onset of normal labor contractions
options.C: Allowing free fetal movement for proper bone and muscle development
options.D: Filtering waste products out of the fetal bloodstream via the mother

explanation: Amniotic fluid acts as a cushion and a swimming pool that lets the baby move its limbs around, helping joints and muscles grow properly. [learn more](BMP210_U4_T5#BMP210_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why is the production of intrinsic factor by the stomach clinically significant?

options.A: It is required for absorbing vitamin B12 further down the gut.

options.C: It stimulates the pancreas to release digestive enzymes.
options.D: It coats the stomach wall to prevent ulcer formation.

explanation: Intrinsic factor binds to vitamin B12 so it can be successfully absorbed in the lower small intestine, preventing pernicious anemia. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T3#BMP118_U1_T3_h3)

question: A postpartum mother experiences severe neck and shoulder tightness after holding her baby in an awkward feeding position for hours. What is the most appropriate initial non-pharmacological care approach?

options.A: Complete bed rest with neck traction for six weeks
options.B: Immediate surgical release of the cervical vertebrae
options.C: Application of ice packs and restriction of all head movement
options.D: Gentle stretching, heat therapy, and ergonomic feeding advice

question: What primary problem defines an intestinal obstruction?

options.A: An infection of the inner lining of the stomach

question: Why is it important to distinguish NANNM from the NMCN?

explanation: Knowing the difference prevents confusion; NANNM fights for your welfare and pay, while the NMCN sets your rules and licenses you. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T5#BMP110_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why does fluid return to the capillary near the venular end?

options.A: Tissue hydrostatic pressure rises higher than the blood pressure

question: A bereaved father angrily accuses the night-shift midwife after a stillbirth. What is the best initial response?

options.A: Ignore him and leave the room
options.B: Listen calmly without taking it personally and acknowledge his distress
options.C: Argue back to prove protocols were followed
options.D: Call security immediately

explanation: Remaining calm helps de-escalate tension while acknowledging that his outburst stems from grief. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T3#BMP120_U5_T3_h3)

question: Why is it necessary to rinse the patient's hair completely free of all soap residue?

options.A: Unrinsed shampoo attracts dangerous bacteria that cause baldness
options.B: Dried soap changes the natural color of the patient's hair strands
options.C: Leftover soap can cause severe scalp dryness, irritation, and itching
options.D: Remaining soap prevents the hair from drying under normal room air

question: What is the main reason for having a reliable running water supply in a health facility?

options.A: To lower the cost of purchasing bottled water for staff
options.B: To keep the hospital floors continuously flooded
options.C: To enable effective hand hygiene between patient contacts

question: Why are smaller doses often effective when administered through the respiratory tract?

options.A: Inhaled drugs are heavier than swallowed pills
options.B: Stomach acids help break down the aerosol particles faster

question: Which of the following describes a clean wound?

options.A: An uninfected surgical wound where sterile tracts are not entered

options.D: A deep tear contaminated with bowel contents

question: Which of the following is a common side effect a mother might feel after taking tramadol?

question: Which antibody can cross the placenta to reach the developing fetus?

question: A patient scheduled for an emergency caesarean section is crying and shaking with fear. What action should the midwife take first?

question: Why is checking urine a standard and helpful tool in primary health care settings?

question: What is a common impact of serious illness on a household?

question: Why do pregnant women often feel looseness in their pelvic joints?

question: Why is brain damage (kernicterus) a major risk for a newborn with severe hemolytic disease?

options.A: Massive red blood cell breakdown releases toxic levels of free bilirubin

question: Which lab result points to a primary gland failure rather than a secondary issue?

question: Which of these is NOT a typical duty of a polyvalent nurse?

question: Why did Florence Nightingale focus so heavily on cleaning hospital wards instead of just treating individual wounds?

question: Which vital sign often changes first when a woman begins to bleed heavily?

question: What does the acronym SBAR stand for in clinical communication?

question: Why is it important to let a patient do parts of their own bath if they are able?

question: What does the abbreviation PONV stand for in surgical care?

question: What is a common sign observed during the depression stage of grief?

question: What is the primary physical benefit of regular hair and scalp hygiene for a bedridden patient?

question: What is a major clinical reason for keeping bed linen tight and wrinkle-free?

question: What happens to fluid movement at the start end of a capillary bed?

question: What is the primary purpose of national professional nursing organizations?

question: A patient has severe itching and swelling from a food allergy, involving antibodies bound to mast cells. Which antibody class is involved?
